arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: General Kagan argued Article I permits the federal civil commitment statute.
Chief Justice Roberts questioned if federal authority persists after criminal justice ends.
Justice Ginsburg asked about the likelihood of detainees staying in federal custody.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the scope of federal power under the Necessary and Proper Clause. It asks if Congress can detain individuals who are no longer under criminal sentence but pose a danger to others.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The government seeks to detain Comstock under federal civil commitment laws.
Comstock seeks release from federal custody and transfer to state authorities.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The government argues Article I permits Congress to enact limited civil commitment statutes.
Comstock argues federal custody authority ends when the criminal sentence expires.
